To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) PCR components such as enhancers and detergents should be avoided in the PCR mixture to obtain optimal detection of nucleic acid by mass spectrometry and that (ii) mismatches located at the last base or the second last at the 3'-end of primers are corrected by the polymerase and are detectable within the amplicons.
the compatibility of the PCR mixture with the mass spectrometry detection is a critical issue that has to be addressed prior to the application of PCR-ICEMS.
(i) the use of enhancers and detergents should be avoided within PCR solutions and (ii) the use of low-quality primers may lead to the detection of truncated amplicons.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a detailed evaluation of the compatibility of a number commercial PCR components with mass spectrometric techniques and the development of a reliable analytical platform for the characterization of PCR amplicons.
the optimization of the solution conditions of the PCR and the development of an efficient analytical platform for the analysis of PCR products by ICEMS.
the optimization of the PCR solution conditions for the efficient mass spectrometry of PCR products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimization of PCR solution conditions should be performed for each individual primer and target combination.
a careful selection of PCR components is essential to avoid the formation of truncated amplicons and the detection of mismatches between primers and the target sequence.
the application of the PCR-ICEMS platform is highly recommended for the characterization of PCR amplicons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a low amount of PCR reagents, especially enhancer and detergency, and the application of proofreading polymerases are crucial for the efficient detection of nucleic acid amplicons by PCR-LC-EIMS.
the use of low cost, but high quality primers and the application of a proofreading DNA polymerase system are essential for successful PCR-ICEMS.
PCR-LC-MS can be used for the detection of nucleic acid amplification products.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the compatibility of PCR and mass spectrometry is limited by the use of enhancers and detergents.
the optimization of the sample solution conditions prior to mass spectrometric analysis is of utmost importance.
PCR-LC-MS can be applied as a fast and efficient method to analyze PCR products and to evaluate the performance of the applied reagents.
